view.name: Mission summary with score
view.description: Immersive-mode end-of-session summary with a three-tier star score (Tiro/Proficiens/Peritus), feedback card, fork-on-GitHub panel and Back to Mission List button.

regions.label: Minimal top-right bar with dashed-outline GitHub Source link and round theme toggle
'Mission Accomplished!' heading with three named star tiers (Tiro/Proficiens/Peritus), earned tier highlighted, italic description
White elevated card with 'Feedback' heading and bullet list of performance comments
Dashed-outline box 'Build Your Own Version' with Fork on GitHub button
Full-width olive 'BACK TO MISSION LIST' button

evidence.note: White rounded card with shadow holding feedback bullets
Dashed outlined card with one primary action (Fork on GitHub)
Star tiers are a system-awarded result, not clickable on live page (clicks did nothing)
Tier row is a level indicator, not a step sequence
Feedback likely model-generated but no marker of AI origin

structure.layout: single centered narrow column (472px) results screen with minimal top-right header, stacked heading, tier indicator, feedback card, promo box and full-width CTA

aesthetics.typography: Libre Baskerville (serif) for headings, tier names and card titles; Nunito (rounded sans) for body, buttons and list text
aesthetics.typeScale: Modest scale: h2 24px/700 serif, h3 19px/700, tier labels ~18px, body 16px/400, buttons 18-20px/800 with uppercase tracked primary CTA, italic 14-16px caption

notes: Warm parchment background (#f5f2eb) with olive green (#5c6b48) accent evokes a classical/Latin feel—tier names are Latin (Tiro, Proficiens, Peritus). Distinctive dashed 2px olive borders on secondary GitHub buttons and a dashed 1px outline on the promo box contrast with the solid white shadowed feedback card. Earned tier shown in black stars + olive serif bold; unearned tiers greyed. Theme toggle is an emoji (💻) in a white circle. Result/completion screen has no codebook entry; proposed 'completion-summary'. Live page showed a different tier (Proficiens) than the capture, suggesting the score is per-session.
